Threat.value: My body reacts to danger before I have even had time to think
I wake during the night to check whether I am safe
I scan for exits as soon as I enter any room or building

Memory.value: The memory feels like it is happening right now rather than something that is over
When I have memories of what happened I sometimes hear things in my head that I heard during the frightening event.
Something in my surroundings can instantly bring back the full memory without warning

Negative Appraisals.value: I have to be on guard all the time
If I think about the event, I will not be able to handle it
I have to be especially careful because you never know what can happen next

issues.item: Triggers: Being Praised: Receiving praise or positive attention
issues.explanation: 'Being praised' is a hard-to-explain trigger in a profile otherwise centered on a life-threatening accident with sensory trigger cues, intrusive reliving, and hypervigilant threat monitoring. Unlike smell or darkness, praise has no evident link to the accident-based memory/threat pattern and stands out as clinically incoherent unless additional interpersonal trauma context were present.

issues.item: Negative Appraisals: Institutional Failure: The people or institutions that should have protected me let me down
issues.explanation: 'Institutional failure' fits betrayal, assault, military, or disaster-response contexts more naturally than a single life-threatening accident in a financial analyst. In this profile the other appraisals focus on danger and inability to cope; this item introduces a qualitatively different blame/betrayal theme that is not supported by the trauma type, trigger pattern, or memory content.

vignette: Kai had always been a man who took pride in his ability to remain calm under pressure. As a financial analyst, he was accustomed to navigating complex spreadsheets and high-stakes deals with ease. But all of that changed on the night of the accident. It happened on a dark stretch of highway, where Kai's car skidded off the road and crashed into a tree. He remembers the sound of screeching tires, the crunch of metal, and the smell of smoke filling his nostrils. As he lay trapped in the wreckage, he heard the distant hum of another car approaching, its headlights casting an eerie glow over the scene. The days that followed were a blur of hospital visits and rehabilitation. But as Kai began to recover physically, he started to notice strange sensations creeping into his daily life. Certain smells - like the scent of gasoline or burning rubber - would transport him back to that fateful night, making his heart racing and his palms sweat. The sound of cars driving by outside his window at night would startle him awake, his mind racing with worst-case scenarios. Kai found himself becoming increasingly hypervigilant, always on the lookout for potential dangers lurking in every shadow. He would scan rooms and buildings for exits, mentally mapping out escape routes "just in case." His wife, Leilani, noticed the change in him too - how he would wake up multiple times a night to check that all the doors and windows were locked, or how he would become agitated when driving through tunnels or dark alleys. Kai's memories of the accident felt disturbingly present, like they could happen again at any moment. He would hear the sound of screeching tires in his head, even when there were no cars around. Sometimes, these auditory flashbacks would be triggered without warning - by a smell, a sound, or simply a dark space that reminded him of that night. As time went on, Kai became more and more adept at avoiding anything that might trigger these memories. He stopped driving at night, opting instead for public transportation or carpooling with colleagues. He avoided going to movies or theaters where the darkness and loud noises might overwhelm him. But despite his best efforts, the memories persisted - haunting him like a constant shadow. Kai's reasoning was simple: if he thought about the accident too much, he wouldn't be able to handle it. Better to avoid thinking about it altogether. But this strategy came at a cost - Kai felt like he was living in a state of perpetual alertness, always waiting for the other shoe to drop. At work, his colleagues began to notice a change in him too. Kai would become distracted during meetings, his eyes darting towards the door as if expecting some unknown threat to burst in. His productivity suffered, and his usually keen financial instincts began to falter. It was only when Kai's boss called him into her office, expressing concern about his performance, that he realized just how much his symptoms had taken over. Leilani, too, sat him down one evening and asked if everything was okay - she'd noticed the toll it was taking on their relationship, how distant and preoccupied he'd become. Kai knew then that he needed help. He couldn't keep living like this - always looking over his shoulder, waiting for danger to strike. As he sat in his therapist's office, recounting the events of that fateful night, Kai felt a glimmer of hope. Maybe, just maybe, he could learn to tame these demons and find some peace again.
